transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you in today?

Um... I guess I'm here because... I keep having these nights. Where I eat... an amount of food that kind of scares me. 

Like, I’ll start with just some leftovers after I finish grading papers, and... I don't know, I just end up going through cereal, and crackers, peanut butter... even whatever snacks I packed for my classroom. It's just... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Can you tell me more about those times when you're eating—do you feel like you can't stop or control what you're doing?

Yeah... I guess so. It’s... once I start, it kind of feels like the reasonable teacher part of me is just watching from the outside. Like I'm telling myself, 'Joan, stop.' But... my hands just keep opening things anyway. I just keep putting food in my mouth until... until I’m painfully full. So, yeah.
Do these eating episodes make you feel embarrassed, guilty, or upset afterward?
Um... yeah. I guess I do. It's... not a great feeling. I just... I don't really like thinking about it after it happens. I just try to go to sleep.
After these episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise a lot more than usual to try to control your weight or how you feel about what you've eaten?

Um... no, I don't... I don't make myself throw up or take anything like that. 

I just... well, if I have a night like that, I just tell myself I can't have breakfast the next day. Or lunch, usually. And I... I try to make up for it after school. I'll just stay out on the running trail for a long time, or... do a lot of yoga. Even if I'm feeling really shaky or tired, I just... I feel like I have to.
Can you tell me if these episodes of eating a large amount of food happen within a short period of time, like within a couple of hours, or does it feel more spread out over the evening?
Um... I guess it's usually kind of quick. Like, I don't really drag it out. It's just... maybe an hour or two. I'm not really sure. I don't look at the clock.
During these episodes, do you feel like you're not in control of your eating, like you can't stop even if you want to?

Um... yeah, I guess so. It's... hard to explain. 

It's like... once I start, the part of me that's, you know, reasonable... the part that's a teacher all day... it's like she's just watching from the outside. Like, telling me to stop. But... I don't. My hands just keep opening packages and... I just keep going until it hurts.
Have these eating episodes been causing you a lot of distress or affecting your daily life in any way, like at work or with relationships?

Um... I mean, I guess it is. It's just... my evenings and weekends kind of end up revolving around... undoing it. 

So, um... I haven't really been seeing my friends much. Even when I do, I'm just... not really present. And... I've been a lot slower with my grading for school. I just spend a lot of energy worrying about... making sure I still seem put-together when I'm in the classroom. It's... yeah. It's a lot.
How often would you say these episodes happen—like, do they occur at least once every week?

Um... yeah. I guess so. For the past few months... it's been rare to have a week go by without at least one night where I eat way more than I meant to. 

And then... I just, um... I have to try and make up for it the next day. Like, I just won't eat while I'm at school... or I'll push myself to go on a really long walk, or do extra yoga. Just to... try and fix it, I guess.
Do you usually eat alone during these episodes because you're embarrassed about how much you're eating?
Um... yeah. I... I don't really do it around anyone else. It's just... it's something I do when I'm by myself.
During these episodes, do you find yourself eating much more rapidly than usual?
Um... I don't know. I haven't really... paid attention to how fast I'm eating. I just... eat.
During these episodes, do you feel a sense that you’ve completely lost control, like you’re not able to stop eating no matter how much you want to?

Um... yeah. I guess so. It's... it's hard to explain. Once I start... it's almost like the reasonable teacher part of me is just watching from the outside, saying, 'Joan, stop.' 

But... I don't. My hands just keep opening things... and I keep putting food in my mouth until I'm... painfully full.
Have you been having these episodes of eating this large amount of food while feeling out of control at least once a week for the past three months?

Um... yeah, I suppose so. For the past few months... I don't think there's been a week where it hasn't happened at least once. I just... I eat way more than I intend to. And then... the next day, I just try to fix it. I'll skip lunch at school, or... I'll force myself to go for a really long walk, or do extra yoga. Just... trying to make up for it, I guess.
